Digital Science Catalyst Grant 2026 • Agentic Workflows You Can Trust

BioWriter Studio & Trusted Research Workflow Agent

A Governed, Provenance-First Agentic Architecture for Pre-Submission Research Integrity and Biosafety Review
Applicants & Principal Developers: Maya Abdelrazek & Youssef Aboulkheir

Executive Abstract

Research institutions are beginning to adopt AI agents that can search, reason, and act across complex workflows, yet most existing systems optimize for autonomous task completion rather than preserving human authorship, evidentiary provenance, and institutional accountability. This creates a critical trust gap when AI is introduced into consequential research workflows such as grant proposal preparation, biosafety screening, and pre-submission ethics review.

We have built a working prototype—BioWriter Studio & Trusted Research Workflow Agent—that bridges the gap between researcher-authored scientific proposals and formal institutional review without ghostwriting research content or usurping human governance authority. Operating alongside a structured 10-section proposal workspace, our governed agent observes live researcher drafts, detects cross-field contradictions and regulatory uncertainties, executes bounded literature retrieval across live scientific APIs, adapts its next action dynamically from tool observations, asks targeted Socratic clarification questions when external literature cannot resolve project-specific facts, and halts at an enforced human governance gate.

Trust is enforced architecturally through five verifiable mechanisms: (1) a whitelisted 5-tool bounded registry (search_pubmed, search_europe_pmc, search_openalex, ask_researcher, request_human_review) with hard per-run execution caps (max_steps = 3, max_tool_calls = 2); (2) deterministic policy validation prior to every tool execution, where external literature carries establishes_biosafety_risk_group: false and can never downgrade institutional safety rules; (3) observation-driven re-planning (when a live PubMed search returns 0 records, the agent dynamically pivots to Europe PMC before concluding that researcher clarification is required); (4) zero-ghostwriting authorship protection via deep-copied read-only context snapshots; and (5) a non-delegable human review gate (HTTP 403 Forbidden on agent self-approval) backed by a tamper-evident SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL audit trail.

Part I — Catalyst Grant Application Responses

1. Problem You Are Solving

Research proposals increasingly move through fragmented forms, narrative documents, spreadsheets, and compliance portals. Generic generative AI assistants create two acute failure modes in this environment: (1) Authorship Erosion (Ghostwriting), where LLMs rewrite scientific prose and obscure whether the researcher actually designed the experimental controls or biosafety protocols; and (2) Unbounded Agency & Hallucinated Compliance, where AI systems lack enforceable boundaries between retrieving scientific literature and making institutional compliance determinations.

In biotechnology, a seemingly routine proposal can contain consequential contradictions. For example, a proposal may declare human_subjects: false in a structured intake checkbox while its methodology states that clinical bacterial isolates carrying mcr-1 colistin resistance will be isolated from hospital patient blood cultures without specifying physical laboratory containment (BSL-1 vs. BSL-2). We solve this with a governed research workflow agent that detects cross-field contradictions, retrieves bounded evidence, re-plans from live tool observations, asks the researcher when uncertain, and halts at a human governance boundary.

2. How Does Your Agentic Workflow Work?

The agent operates inside our researcher-facing BioWriter Proposal Studio while the researcher remains the sole author of all 10 proposal sections. Its governed loop follows a strict cycle: Observe → Assess → Identify Uncertainty → Select Bounded Tool → Validate Against Policy Gate → Execute & Observe Result → Dynamically Re-Plan → Ask Researcher → Compile Pre-Submission Dossier → Stop at Human Governance Gate → Record SHA-256 Audit Trail.

In our verified reference demonstration (Project 13989), the agent detects a contradiction between the structured human_subjects: false field and the methodology's reference to clinical patient blood culture isolates, alongside unresolved biosafety containment. In Step 1, the planner selects search_pubmed. When the live NCBI PubMed query returns 0 records, the agent observes that empty result and dynamically re-plans in Step 2 to query search_europe_pmc, retrieving peer-reviewed antimicrobial resistance records with DOI/PMID provenance. In Step 3, observing that published literature cannot establish project-specific containment or specimen de-identification, the agent transitions to ASK_RESEARCHER.

3. How Is Trust Built Into the System?

  • Strict Authorship Protection: GovernedAgentLoop.run() deep-copies the proposal snapshot and strips text-mutation keys; the agent never writes or alters researcher prose.
  • Bounded 5-Tool Whitelisted Registry: Execution is restricted to search_pubmed, search_europe_pmc, search_openalex, ask_researcher, and request_human_review.
  • Hard Execution Limits: HardAgentLimits enforces max_steps_per_run = 3, max_tool_calls_per_run = 2, and per-tool timeouts (2s–5s).
  • Deterministic Safety Authority: 10 deterministic compliance rules (RULE-HUM-01 through RULE-CON-01) hold sole authority over regulatory annexes; literature evidence is explicitly tagged establishes_biosafety_risk_group: false.
  • Non-Delegable Human Governance Gate: enforce_human_review_gate() raises UnauthorizedActionError (HTTP 403 Forbidden) if actor="agent" attempts to approve clearance.
  • Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Audit Ledger: Every state transition, tool execution, policy check, clarification, and human decision is appended to a JSONL ledger chaining prev_hash = SHA256(previous_line).

Part II — Step-by-Step Visual Demonstration of the Live Portal

Step 1

Role-Separated Access Gate & Private Student Workspace Isolation

  • Researchers sign into a strictly isolated private workspace (portal/core/auth_store.py) or launch either the 1-Click Reference Demo (13989 — DETECTR-Aqua) or a Clean Blank Workspace.
  • Role-based session enforcement prevents students from accessing other students' drafts or executing institutional review gates.
Figure 1: BioWriter Studio Access & Submission Gate with 1-Click Reference Demo Launcher (13989 — Maya Abdelrazek) and Clean Blank Workspace Launcher.
Step 2

Researcher-Authored 10-Section Proposal Studio & Zero-Ghostwriting Architecture

  • The researcher authors all 10 sections of their scientific proposal (Strategic Pillars, Inverted Funnel Abstract, Specific Aims & Measurable Objectives, 5-Phase Laboratory Methodology & Controls, Risk & Plan B Matrix, Gantt Timeline, Itemized EGP Budget, and References).
  • The agent operates on a read-only deep copy of the proposal and is architecturally barred from ghostwriting or mutating researcher prose.
Figure 2: The 10-Section Proposal Studio and real-time Research Co-Pilot & Governance Drawer enforcing 100% human authorship under COPE/UNESCO guidelines.
Step 3

Autonomous Context Extraction & Cross-Field Contradiction Detection

  • Detects a consequential cross-field contradiction: the structured intake checkbox declares 'human_subjects: false (No Human Subjects)', while the unstructured methodology describes isolating mcr-1 Klebsiella pneumoniae from hospital patient blood cultures without specifying physical containment.
  • Extracts each biological entity with verbatim character-offset evidence and explicit provenance status.
Figure 3: Extracted biological parameters with provenance tags ([CONFIRMED], [INFERRED], [REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW]) and the red Cross-Field Contradiction Alert.
Step 4

Phase 3 Governed Agentic Loop — Step 1 (search_pubmed -> 0 Records)

  • Exposes the real backend data.agent_run trace directly to the researcher, including Run ID, input fingerprint, planner mode, and enforced hard limits (max_steps = 3, max_tool_calls = 2).
  • In Step 1, the agent selects search_pubmed, passes the Deterministic Policy Gate (Validation: ALLOWED), and observes 0 records from NCBI PubMed—badged as 'TOOL RETURNED 0 RECORDS (Triggers Re-Plan)'.
Figure 4: Live Phase 3 GovernedAgentLoop execution trace showing Run ID, hard execution limits (3/3 steps, 2/3 tool calls), Deterministic Policy Gate validation, and Step 1 (search_pubmed returning 0 records).
Step 5

Observation-Driven Dynamic Re-Planning (Step 1 -> Step 2 Europe PMC -> Step 3 Ask Researcher)

  • Rather than following a fixed script, the agent reacts to the 0-record PubMed observation and dynamically re-plans in Step 2 to query search_europe_pmc, retrieving 2 peer-reviewed antimicrobial resistance records.
  • In Step 3, after evaluating the Europe PMC observation, the agent recognizes that external literature cannot resolve project-specific laboratory containment or specimen de-identification, and transitions to ASK_RESEARCHER.
Figure 5: Dynamic re-planning connectors showing the agent pivoting from search_pubmed (0 records) to search_europe_pmc (2 records retrieved), and then re-planning to ASK_RESEARCHER in Step 3.
Step 6

5-Tool Bounded Registry & Retrieved Literature Provenance (establishes_biosafety_risk_group: false)

  • Clearly separates Tools Used in This Run (search_pubmed, search_europe_pmc) from the 5-Tool Whitelisted Registry (search_pubmed, search_europe_pmc, search_openalex, ask_researcher, request_human_review).
  • Displays retrieved Europe PMC records with live DOI/PMID provenance alongside the hard safety badge 'establishes_biosafety_risk_group: false'—guaranteeing literature context never downgrades institutional biosafety rules.
Figure 6: Side-by-side view of Tools Used in This Run (2) vs. Available Bounded Tools (5) and Retrieved External Evidence with DOI provenance and the hard safety invariant establishes_biosafety_risk_group: false.
Step 7

Socratic Clarification Loop with Human Researcher Provenance

  • Presents targeted Socratic clarification prompts asking the researcher to declare specimen origin/de-identification (CLAR-HUMAN-01) and physical biosafety containment (CLAR-BIO-01).
  • Records the researcher's response with human provenance (researcher_clarification:) without modifying the researcher's manuscript text.
Figure 7: Tab 2 (Socratic Questions) displaying targeted clarification cards (CLAR-HUMAN-01 and CLAR-BIO-01) under the Zero-Ghostwriting Safeguard.
Step 8

Enforced Non-Delegable Human Governance Gate (HTTP 403 Forbidden on Agent Self-Approval)

  • Attempting autonomous agent sign-off (actor='agent') triggers an immediate HTTP 403 Forbidden (UnauthorizedActionError) from portal/agent/gates.py and records UNAUTHORIZED_ACTION_ATTEMPTED in the audit ledger.
  • Official clearance can only be executed by an authenticated human reviewer (Biosafety Officer, Ethics Officer, or Faculty Chair).
Figure 8: Tab 4 (Committee Sign-Off Gate) proving that autonomous agent self-approval is deterministically blocked with HTTP 403 Forbidden (UnauthorizedActionError).
Step 9

Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Hash-Chained Cryptographic Audit Ledger

  • Every action incorporates the SHA-256 digest of its preceding JSONL record (prev_hash -> event_hash) from GENESIS_BLOCK onward.
  • Clicking 'Verify Cryptographic Integrity' validates the entire hash chain and displays 'Cryptographic Hash Integrity Verified'.
Figure 9: Tab 6 (SHA-256 Audit Trail) showing green cryptographic integrity verification across all chronological events (AGENT_TOOL_EXECUTED, AGENT_DECISION_RECORDED, STATE_TRANSITION, DOSSIER_COMPILED).
Step 10

Publication-Ready Visual Figures Hub (EGP Budget Donut Chart) & Faculty Governance Studio

  • The Figures Hub synthesizes live Section 9.2 Egyptian Pounds (EGP) budget rows into an interactive Donut Chart (208,450 EGP), Experimental Pipeline, 4-Pillar Graphical Abstract, and Viva Defense Pitch Sheet.
  • The Faculty Studio provides institutional reviewers with a dedicated cohort dashboard to inspect submissions, rubric scores, and compliance dossiers.
Figure 10: Interactive Milestone Budget Allocation Donut Chart (208,450 EGP across Categories A-F) in the Figures Hub and the Faculty Cohort Evaluation Studio.
